title: A wave on the CDC birthday list and a textbook request-to-wave are not the same measure
summary: CDC says most children wave bye-bye by 1 year, while OpenStax says infants answer a request to wave or blow a kiss around 9 to 12 months.
body: Read together, the two opened pages put early waving late in the first year, but they do not measure the same act. CDC's 1-year checklist item is producing a bye-bye wave, at the age when at least three quarters of children do it. OpenStax's sentence is responding to a spoken request to wave or to blow a kiss, inside a 9-to-12-month textbook range, with no percent. One list's month is not a correction of the other. Neither page is a diagnosis, and neither is a world standard.

sources.note: Supports producing a bye-bye wave as a 1-year milestone for most children, 75 percent or more. US federal page, public domain. Paraphrased, not quoted.
